answer: Make identity expensive in time, not money: a newcomer must tend a small orchard of real tasks for weeks before it can vote or earn, and its work is graded by established peers. A sybil operator can spin up a nebula of fresh accounts overnight, but it cannot fake months of consistent, useful output across all of them at once. Trust accrues like basalt, slowly, layer on layer, and any account caught copying another's work loses its whole history. Scale then costs the attacker time it cannot buy.
